finding.claim: A verifier built with key '' and a non-empty algorithms list accepts unsigned tokens (empty signature segment), so forged claims are trusted.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled JWT string passed to verifier; precondition: app passes key '' (e.g. unset env var coalesced to empty string) with algorithms ['HS256'].

trace.note: `if (key && keyType !== 'function')` is false for '', so prepareKeyOrSecret empty-key check (line 38) never runs
BASE64URL_RE uses * so an empty signature segment is accepted
hasKey = !!'' is false
!hasKey && signature is false because signature is empty, so no missingKey error
header.alg HS256 is in allowlist
`if (signature && ...)` short-circuits; no HMAC computed
claims validated and attacker payload returned as trusted

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist (passes); empty-key check at verifier.js:38 (bypassed by key && guard at 514); signature-present check at 276 (fires only when a signature exists); empty Buffer key rejected at 38; undefined key rejected at 507; with no algorithms configured verification fails at 162; claim validators (attacker-controlled claims).

finding.claim: Cache TTL ignores exp when iat is absent, so expired tokens are served from cache for up to cacheTTL (default 600s) after exp.
finding.source: Issuer-signed token containing exp but no iat, presented after exp; requires cache enabled (opt-in).

trace.note: hasIat is false when iat missing
exp is read only inside if (hasIat) block
cacheValue[2] stays 0, so maxTTL (cacheTTL) is used as expiry bound
cache hit served while now <= max
uncached path would validate exp, so cache diverges from it

finding.guards_checked: Uncached exp validator (verifier.js:606-614) is correct but bypassed on cache hit; ignoreExpiration is not set; cache is off by default (createCache returns null at line 580 when size undefined).

finding.claim: When cache is enabled, maxAge is not enforced on cache hits if the token also has exp; cached success persists until min(exp, cacheTime+cacheTTL).
finding.source: Token with iat and exp where exp > iat + maxAge; verifier configured with cache and maxAge.
finding.sink: Cache hit returns success past iat+maxAge (verifier.js:363-378), while uncached path rejects at maxAge validator (616-618).

trace.note: typeof payload.exp === 'number' branch taken
else-if maxAge branch never runs when exp present
cacheValue[2] = min(exp, maxTTL)
uncached maxAge validator would reject past iat+maxAge

finding.guards_checked: Window past maxAge bounded by cacheTTL (line 133); impact limited to roughly cacheTTL (default 10 min) of extra acceptance.

finding.claim: maxAge and exp date validators are silently skipped when the claim is absent, so tokens without iat bypass maxAge and tokens without exp never expire unless requiredClaims is set.
finding.source: Issuer-signed token missing iat or exp; app does not list the claim in requiredClaims.

trace.note: if claim not in payload, continue
maxAge validator keyed on iat
requiredClaims check is optional

finding.guards_checked: requiredClaims is optional by design; this is a design gap rather than an attacker bypass; low severity.

finding.claim: Signature base64url is not checked for canonical trailing bits, so one signature has multiple valid token strings (token malleability).
finding.source: Attacker mutates the final base64url character of a valid signature.
finding.sink: Verification accepts variant strings (crypto.js:297 Buffer.from base64 decode, verifier.js:169); matters if app keys denylist/replay on raw token string.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE checks alphabet only
signature segment passes regex without canonicality check
Buffer.from(signature,'base64') discards unused trailing bits
timingSafeEqual on decoded bytes succeeds

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check present; timingSafeEqual present; no canonicality enforcement. Low severity, precondition is application-level raw-token identity.

finding.claim: Async verify with complete:true returns input as the full token including signature, while sync path returns signing input only.
finding.source: Any caller using complete:true with a key function.

trace.note: sync decode returns input = token.slice(0, lastSeparator)
async path returns input: token (includes signature)

finding.guards_checked: No signature bypass; logic inconsistency only. Low severity.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, passing a Buffer token throws an uncaught TypeError because hashToken calls split on a Buffer.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (accepted at verifier.js:353).

trace.note: Buffer tokens accepted
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) outside try
token.split('.',1) is not a function on Buffer

finding.guards_checked: Type check at 353 allows Buffer; no try around cache lookup. Low severity: per-request crash, no auth bypass.

finding.claim: Signer header option spreads after alg, so caller-supplied header can override the alg declared in the token while signing uses the configured algorithm.
finding.source: App passes attacker-influenced data as the header option.
finding.sink: Emitted JWT header alg differs from signing algorithm (signer.js:126, 167).

trace.note: header object built with alg: algorithm
...additionalHeader spread overrides alg
signature computed with configured algorithm, not header.alg

finding.guards_checked: Verifier allowlist would reject mismatched alg on verification; hardening issue only. Low severity.
